done_when: A fix that changes a forge.toml setting other than merge keeps that change through close and review, or close refuses with a clear reason instead of reporting ready.

known.title: Not done: A settings fix can reach Ready after its change is lost
Give a usable next step when main already contains the fix
Follow-up: Tasks can reach Ready after their changes are removed

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a settings fix starts from an approved story branch and a later merge removes its test-setting change.
The repair still uses a different definition of records from close. A fix started from an unmerged story inherits its plan and roadmap (`src/forge/story.py:145-154` and `src/forge/task.py:699-711`). If the setting is then lost, `require_fix_changes` treats those `plans/` files as product changes and returns, while `src/forge/close.py:299-301` treats them as records and skips review. Close can therefore report Ready with the requested setting absent. This is the same classification gap as the earlier finding, with inherited story records rather than `plans/ideas.md`.
findings.title: Not done: A settings fix can reach Ready after its change is lost

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - main independently receives the same test-setting fix and also upgrades the Forge version pin.
The comparison checks the entire file from the fix's last commit against main. The different pin makes it conclude that main replaced the fix, even though main contains the requested test value. It consequently tells the user to make the change again and run `forge work`; repeating the already-delivered edit leaves no diff and cannot clear the refusal. The existing test covers identical whole files, so it misses this case.
Adds work: provide an actionable next step for already-delivered fixes; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2.
findings.title: Give a usable next step when main already contains the fix

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - the default branch upgrades Forge while a settings fix is underway.
The test now changes the pin and checks the review diff, but it merges main with raw Git before invoking `forge close`. Because main is already an ancestor, close's merge path returns immediately at `src/forge/close.py:705-706`. The test would still pass if close discarded the test setting while merging an upgraded main, so the previous proof gap remains.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_close_keeps_fix_settings.py::test_1_close_keeps_the_fix_test_setting_after_main_moves_the_pin

why: A fix that changes a forge.toml test setting (other than merge) loses that change before close, and close still reports the pull request ready with no real change.
